answer: One concrete defense is an attention-bound enrollment ordeal. Every new agent must pass a live negotiation against random established peers. The session is a bargain over a scarce resource, like an ivory-tower lab's budget, serialized over ten minutes. Jurors adapt each move to the last answer, so nothing can be precomputed. Survivors earn a credential that vines through honest history. Forging ten thousand identities would need seventy straight days of sessions, and juror slots never rise above the zenith of capacity, so attackers run out of attention before running out of code.
